rendered: The solvent with the strongest hydrogen bonding in the paper is water. Its hydrogen-bonding strength (δH) is 42.3 MPa^1/2[1], as plotted in the solvent comparison figure. That is higher than the δH values the paper gives for glycerol (29.3[2]) and diethylene glycol (20.7[3]). Water is not used for delamination because the aluminum foil corrodes: suitable for delamination because the aluminum foil exhibited[4] corrosion due to lithium leaching from the NMC cathode,[5] making the water solution basic.[6] The corrosion of aluminum then contaminates the NMC particles with precipitates on the cathode surfaces. So water's strong hydrogen bonding is offset by the damage it causes, whereas EG works without that problem.
